_about: Real human anatomy for the cad-designer golfer (Christelle, 2026-10-30: 'take real human anatomy into account and how muscles really move'). Lengths in metres for the source's own mean stature; cad3d scales them to the golfer's height. Every number names its source; 'estimate' marks the few that have none.

sources.de_leva_1996: de Leva P. Adjustments to Zatsiorsky-Seluyanov's segment inertia parameters. J Biomech 1996;29(9):1223-30, Table 4, males (stature 1.741 m). https://doi.org/10.1016/0021-9290(95)00178-6
sources.ansur_2012: ANSUR II anthropometric survey of US Army personnel, 2010-2012, 4,082 men, mean stature 1.756 m (public working database). https://ph.health.mil/topics/workplacehealth/ergo/Pages/Anthropometric-Database.aspx
sources.aaos_rom: AAOS normal joint range of motion, as tabulated in Hendriks et al., Plast Reconstr Surg Glob Open 2020 (supplement). https://cdn-links.lww.com/permalink/prsgo/b/prsgo_8_6_2020_04_17_hendriks_gox-d-20-00155r2_sdc1.pdf
sources.jssm_2018: Golf address posture vs ball position, 11 male KPGA pros, five-iron: trunk flexion 41.5 deg at the reference ball position. J Sports Sci Med 2018;17(4):589. https://jssm.org/jssm-17-589.xml-Fulltext
sources.psu_rotation: Penn State golf biomechanics: at the top of the backswing the pelvis is usually turned about 35-55 deg and the torso about 85-110 deg. https://golf.psu.edu/interactives/rotation
sources.xfactor_studies: X-factor (torso minus pelvis) at the top: 53.4 +/- 10.0 deg (women, driver); Zheng et al. about 58-60 deg. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3362989
sources.kinematic_sequence: Proximal-to-distal kinematic sequence in the downswing: pelvis, then thorax, then lead arm, then club. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3362989
sources.bechler_1995: Bechler, Jobe, Pink, Perry et al. 1995, EMG of the hip and knee in 16 golfers: in the forward swing the trail hip extensors and abductors and the lead adductor magnus start the pelvic rotation; the lead hamstrings hold a flexed knee as a stable base. https://www.bisp-surf.de/Record/PU199606108067
sources.jobe_perry_pink_1989: Jobe, Perry and Pink 1989, shoulder EMG in the golf swing: latissimus dorsi active in the downswing, pectoralis major and subscapularis at impact (as cited in the 2012 review).
sources.emg_review_2012: EMG variables during the golf swing, literature review of 19 studies, J Electromyogr Kinesiol 2012: pectoralis major, subscapularis and latissimus dorsi on both sides peak in the acceleration phase; the trail erector spinae is highly active in acceleration; the obliques are moderate to low. https://sponet.de/sponet/Record/4026714?lng=en
sources.muscle_volume: Skeletal muscle keeps its volume as it changes length, so a shortening muscle gets thicker (a belly radius goes as 1/sqrt(length)).
sources.forearm_rom: Forearm pronation 80 deg and supination 80 deg, from a table of normal joint ranges (also the figure usually quoted as AAOS). https://www.sncc.ca/resources/Documents/Dragon%20Boat/2024%20CCWCs/range%20of%20motion%20normal%20values.pdf
sources.lesiuta_slides: Lesiuta E., 'A Biomechanical Analysis of the Golf Swing' (course presentation EE3BA3, from Christelle 2026-10-30). Secondary: set-up trunk flexed 45 deg at the hips and trail shoulder tilted down 16 deg (citing Hosea & Gatt 1996); X-factor about 50 deg (citing Meister); lead elbow extended and trail arm abducted 75-90 deg at the top; trail arm adducts in the downswing; late uncocking adds up to 9% club-head speed; follow-through decelerates with eccentric muscle work; L4-L5 load about 6x body weight in the downswing.
sources.cole_grimshaw_2016: Cole MH, Grimshaw PN. The biomechanics of the modern golf swing: implications for lower back injuries. Sports Med 2016;46(3):339-51. Thorax turns more than the pelvis to pre-stretch the trunk muscles (stored elastic energy); skilled golfers slide the pelvis towards the target in the downswing. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26604102/
sources.drvn_blog: DRVN Golf, 'Golf swing fundamentals' (coaching article, cites no research): the lead hip clears first, then torso, arms and club; hands slightly ahead at impact. Used only where a study agrees. https://drvngolf.com/blog/golf-swing-fundamentals

muscle_activity._scale: 2 = high, 1 = moderate. Only what the sources say; a phase with no source shows no firing muscles.
